title: Law-Uniform Safety and Welfare Regret When Policy Feasibility Is Unknown
banked_reason: The omitted Stoye (2012) derives exact normal/Bernoulli test-level treatment rules and Type-I/Type-II regret tradeoffs, making the solved single-slack Neyman-Pearson frontier a routine reparameterization below the field-tier floor.
gap_reasons: The omitted Stoye (2012), Statistical Treatment Choice Based on Asymmetric Minimax Regret Criteria, is a closer published comparator: it derives exact normal/Bernoulli test-level treatment rules and Type-I/Type-II regret tradeoffs, making the solved single-slack Neyman--Pearson frontier presently a routine reparameterization and below the field-tier floor.
proof_attempt_summary: The original hexagon direction overlapped a live project. The revised angle derived a scalar exact-safety and regret frontier, but the final reviewer identified a close Stoye (2012) predecessor and rated its published novelty below the field floor. No D0 proof or Lean formalization began; a new field-level project would need a genuinely two-slack, constraint-sensitive theorem with matching lower and upper values.
tldr: Exact law-uniform safety can destroy statistical adaptation when harm coefficients or budgets are unknown. In a finite experiment with six arm counts and two independent budget-audit counts, common support forces every zero-error rule over the global public box to use only \(S_\cap=\{q^0\}\). A three-cell causal-policy embedding has the distinct submodel intersection \(S_{\cap,0}=\{q^0,q^O\}\) and a safe welfare oracle that switches across an arbitrarily small change in one Bernoulli mean. Safety at level \(1-\delta\) imposes the exact boundary size restriction \(P_{\eta(0)}^{(n)}\{D_n=q^S\}\le\delta\); randomized Neyman--Pearson inversion then gives the explicit finite-sample power \(\pi_{n,\delta}(h)\), its matching regret bound, and the sharp limit \(C_\delta(h)\). The solved frontier is a generic unknown-feasibility result: deleting either overlapping constraint leaves the oracle switch, statistic, optimal rule, and constant unchanged. Unlike Stoye's exact minimax regret and Hirano--Porter's local treatment rules, the frontier is generated by law-varying feasibility. Genuinely overlapping adaptation with two nonparallel binding slack directions and joint error allocation remains the open question.
gap: Safe causal-policy methods establish individual no-harm, baseline-improvement, posterior chance-safety, or asymptotic reward guarantees, but none of these conditions is a uniform frequentist constraint over a safe set that changes with the data-generating law. Ordinary minimax-regret treatment choice also fixes the feasible action set. The unresolved headline object is the sharp welfare cost of learning a feasibility boundary; the further overlap-specific object requires several nonparallel binding slack directions.
fill: The project proves the global public-box support equivalence and a separate restricted-submodel support lemma, embeds an unknown-feasibility oracle switch in a three-cell causal policy problem, and derives the safety-induced finite-sample size restriction, exact power \(\pi_{n,\delta}(h)\), matching regret bound, and local constant \(C_\delta(h)\). An explicit scope proposition proves that deleting either constraint leaves this frontier unchanged. A fully specified simultaneous confidence-inner rule is supporting deployment material, while a distinct open question reserves the genuinely overlapping case.
